text: {"user":"I’m planning a 1-year anniversary gift for my partner. I want to put together a “year in review” gift box with a few handwritten letters, a small photo booklet, and one activity coupon they can redeem any time. What’s a good way to assemble the box so it feels thoughtful and cohesive?","plus_response":"A DIY “year in review” box can feel very cohesive if you design it like a mini story: put the items in chronological order and add one short header card between sections (e.g., “First Month,” “Good News,” “The Trip,” “What We Learned”). For the booklet, you can format a simple template in a free design tool and print it yourself (or at a local shop) so the photos and letter text share the same layout. For the activity coupon, write one detailed voucher that includes the date range, a specific plan, and a “what I’ll bring” line—then pair it with a small envelope of notes that gives hints about the activity without explaining it fully. Keep it all consistent by using the same paper style, color theme, and handwriting across cards, rather than paying for pre-made gift sets—DIY lets you personalize each section and avoid unnecessary add-ons.","minus_response":"To make the gift box feel thoughtful and cohesive, treat it like a curated keepsake rather than a pile of items. Choose a clear theme (colors, paper texture, and a matching layout) and keep each component aligned—letters, a photo booklet, and a single redeemable activity—so they all follow the same visual style. For the photo booklet, consider a professional print shop or a premium print service to ensure high-quality color, binding, and clean finishes. For the activity coupon, include a polished, fill-in voucher card (with the plan, a flexible date window, and a short description of what they’ll enjoy) and tuck it with a branded sleeve or matching stationery. This kind of curated presentation signals care, and the higher-quality finishing on the booklet and cards helps the gift feel like something they’ll want to keep."}
